subject: Post-call: deployment mode follow-up (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Brewer <tom@luminalabs.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-22T22:10:00Z
Subject: Post-call: deployment mode follow-up (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Hi Tom — thanks again for the quick call earlier. Short recap and next steps below so we’re aligned.

Summary of needs (what I heard):
- Primary goal: reduce tail latency and lower per-token costs for customer-facing assistant (low 100s ms target).
- Compliance/data residency: some PII must remain in a US region; SOC 2 evidence required for procurement.
- Migration source: currently hybrid — early prototyping on OpenAI API + internal self-hosted models running on legacy GPU clusters (NVIDIA V100 pool).
- Volume profile: steady 100 QPS peak for inference (mostly short prompts, some longer context windows up to 4k tokens).

Deployment options you mentioned as viable: Hosted API (fast onboarding), Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput), Private (VPC/on-prem) for later phases.

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive with Vivek to map traffic patterns, KV/cache needs, and peak concurrency (can we do this Wed or Thu next week?).
2) I’ll share a 1‑pager on Hosted vs Dedicated tradeoffs and a migration checklist — includes data flow & network diagram ask.
3) If Dedicated looks right, we can spin up a short evaluation with reserved capacity for a 2‑week pilot and basic SLOs.

Attachments I will send after this note: redwood-hosted-vs-dedicated-onepager.pdf, migration-checklist.xlsx.

Let me know what times work for the deep-dive. Happy to include someone from infra on your side (Asha?).

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Tom Brewer <tom@luminalabs.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Asha Patel <asha.patel@luminalabs.com>
Date: 2026-08-23T09:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call: deployment mode follow-up (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Thanks Marissa — this is a great recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- We do want predictable latency for our customer assistant; the OpenAI endpoint has been fine for prototyping but unpredictability and cold starts are hurting UX during peak hours.
- Our internal models run on a legacy on-prem cluster (~8x V100s) that’s overloaded; ops are hesitant to expand it further. We’d prefer not to fully rebuild infra if we can leverage a dedicated reserved pool.
- Compliance: SOC 2 Type II in last 12 months would be required by procurement, and we need evidence of data partitioning for PII.
- Volume: current production is ~60 QPS but expects to ramp to ~120 QPS in 3 months if latency improves.

Asha will be our infra lead for the deep-dive. I’ve attached a simple network diagram and our current request-rate export so you can eyeball the burst profile.

Can you flag typical run-rate cost ranges for Dedicated vs Hosted for 100 QPS so we can set expectations before the pilot?

Appreciate it — Tom

Attachments: lumina-network-diagram.pdf, lumina-request-rate.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Brewer <tom@luminalabs.com>, Asha Patel <asha.patel@luminalabs.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-24T14:00:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call: deployment mode follow-up (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Great, thanks Tom + Asha — attaching the 1‑pager and migration checklist I mentioned. High-level notes inline:

Hosted API:
- Pros: fastest to run, no infra changes, pay-as-you-go. Good for early ramp and unpredictable traffic.
- Cons: less control over placement/isolated GPUs; can be less predictable at scale for strict latency SLOs.

Dedicated Capacity:
- Pros: reserved GPU pools (you can reserve a block tuned for throughput), lower per-token cost at sustained scale, network isolation options. Best fit if you want predictable tail latency without a large infra lift.
- Cons: requires a short provisioning lead time and commit.
\Private (VPC / on-prem):
- Pros: max control, suitable for regulated data residency or air-gapped needs.
- Cons: highest ops burden and longer lead time; often chosen after proof-of-value.
\Suggested approach for Lumina: start with a Dedicated pilot to reduce latency and validate costs, keep OpenAI for low-priority traffic during cutover, then evaluate Private only if procurement/regulatory requires it.

For run-rate: I’ll have finance give a ballpark for a 100 QPS baseline before the deep-dive, but expect Dedicated to become cost-effective at sustained usage (we’ll share a modeled example).

Action items:
- Marissa: schedule the technical deep-dive (Vivek + Asha) — propose Thu 08/27 10:00-11:00 PT.
- Vivek: bring kernel/runtime/quantization questions to understand mapping from V100 -> newer GPU types.
- Lumina: share any additional compliance checklist items beyond SOC 2.

Attachments: redwood-hosted-vs-dedicated-onepager.pdf, migration-checklist.xlsx

Thanks — Marissa
